newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - ASDA sales momentum continues.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - ASDA sales momentum continues.

text.p: British supermarket retailer ASDA Group Plc is likely to check in a rise in year profits and dividend when it reports results on June 26 and should show its momentum continuing, analysts said.

"They could be a very good set of results. ASDA's had a pretty good last few months and start to the year, we are looking for a fairly confident statement on prospects," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
ASDA's annual pretax profits are seen between 344-355 million stg, up from 304.6 million a year ago and it should pay out a dividend of 2.83-3.1 pence per share compared with 2.65 pence.
ASDA, turned round from heavy debts under the leadership of the charismatic Archie Norman, currently chairman, has cornered a niche in the market for quality at low prices.
Analysts said that although the company's surging sales rises of its recovery period are likely to have slowed, ASDA should still be pushing turnover.
"New store openings, a recovery in petrol sales, increased sales of own-label and non-food items have all helped to boost sales," the analyst said.
ASDA does not usually provide a current trading statement with results.
Analysts said Allan Leighton, the new chief executive who has been Norman's deputy for several years, is seen as a safe pair of hands and likely to retain reforms.
"ASDA's likely to reiterate its stance of simple food selling, without diversification into financial services like some of its competitors," the analyst said.
ASDA is the only one of the big four UK supermarkets which does not have a nationwide loyalty card.
